entities.summary: Demetrios Angelos Doukas Palaiologos (fl. 14th century) was a Byzantine prince who played a significant role in the Byzantine succession crisis of 1350-1352. He was the second son of Emperor Andronikos II Palaiologos and his wife Irene of Montferrat, and his early life was marked by intrigue and power struggles within the imperial family. Following the death of his elder brother Andronikos III, Demetrios briefly seized power in 1350, but his reign was short-lived due to his inability to secure the support of key nobles and the opposition of the powerful John Kantakouzenos. As a result, Demetrios was eventually forced to abdicate in favor of John, who went on to become one of the most influential figures in Byzantine history. Demetrios's legacy is largely overshadowed by that of his contemporaries, but his story provides valuable insights into the complexities of Byzantine politics and the challenges faced by the empire during its final decades.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Demetrios Angelos Doukas Palaiologos played a significant role in the Byzantine succession crisis of 1350-1352, marking the beginning of a new era in the empire's history. His legacy is largely overshadowed by that of his contemporaries, but his story provides valuable insights into the complexities of Byzantine politics and the challenges faced by the empire during its final decades.
